subject: Post-call: model-fit evals & regression concern — proposed pin/rollback options
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Tran <olivia.tran@novacredit.com>, Novacredit SRE <sre@novacredit.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: model-fit evals & regression concern — proposed pin/rollback options

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the 8/22 call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move the eval to a short pilot: 

Summary of needs (from call)
- Primary workload: credit-decision assistant generating applicant-facing rationale (high safety/compliance bar)
- Perf targets: <= 1200ms median generation, <2% hallucination on policy-focused prompts
- Traffic: 200 qps peak expected for Tier-1 flows
- Data constraints: PII redaction, audit logs retention for 365 days

What we shared (attachments/links)
- Eval pack: novacredit_eval_pack_v1.zip — contains benchmark prompts, prompt_set_customer_v3.json, sample transcripts and measurement harness (Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bEvalPackNovacredit)
- Benchmarks: quick perf table we ran across our catalog (see Drive folder)

Initial model recommendations
- Recommended baseline: redwood-beta/seqclarity-v1.2 (good safety curve + latency)
- Candidate higher-quality variant: seqclarity-v1.4 (better language fluency but we flagged a safety delta in our internal tests)

Regression concern raised on call
- Olivia noted a recent regression where a production update to seqclarity-v1.4 showed an uptick in factual hallucinations on policy prompts. Novacredit sent a couple of examples offline. Marcus and engineering will triage.

Proposed immediate actions
1) Marcus to run a quick diff between v1.2 and v1.4 on the Novacredit prompt set (attached diff_report_v1.4_vs_v1.2.pdf). ETA: EOD 8/22.
2) If regression confirmed, we recommend pinning Novacredit's traffic to seqclarity-v1.2 while we canary-fix v1.4 on a tiny percentage of traffic. Pinning avoids outage risk.
3) Camila to coordinate a short (30m) call 8/24 to agree rollback/pinning and timeline; Novacredit SRE to share the logs you mentioned (regression_log_20260821.txt)

Next step: please confirm availability for 30m on Monday 8/24 between 10:00–15:00 PT.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-call: model-fit evals & regression concern — proposed pin/rollback options

Thanks Camila — appreciated summary. We're attaching the two offending examples and a small log excerpt (regression_log_20260821.txt). Quick notes from our side: 

- The failure mode: when the model is asked to summarize an applicant's adverse history, v1.4 produced confident statements that are not in the supplied source docs (false attributions). This is a compliance risk.
- We can tolerate slight latency increases but not quality degradation here.
- We already have a short list of internal prompts that exercise policy checks — I attached them.

Request: Please make pin/rollback recommendations formally in writing before we touch prod. If pinning is straightforward, we'd prefer that while Redwood investigates.

Availability: 8/24 11:30–12:30 PT works for me.

Olivia Tran
Director, Product Integrity | Novacredit
olivia.tran@novacredit.com

Attachments: regression_log_20260821.txt

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Tran <olivia.tran@novacredit.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T17:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model-fit evals & regression concern — proposed pin/rollback options

Hi Olivia — I ran a fast diff over your prompt set and the examples you sent. Summary below (top-level):

- Observations: v1.4 increases generation diversity but a small subset (~0.8% of prompts in your eval pack) show hallucinated facts compared to v1.2. See diff_report_v1.4_vs_v1.2.pdf (attached) for examples and token-level logits for one failing case.
- Root cause hypothesis: v1.4's updated decoding bias and factual calibration layer was tuned for downstream helpfulness, which can surface confabulation on heavily-constrained policy prompts.

Immediate mitigations I can enact today (low-friction):
1) Pining option (recommended): Configure your production route to target model "seqclarity-v1.2" explicitly (we can pin at the model-version level in the route config). No code changes required on your side; Redwood will honor the pinned version until you opt-in to upgrades.
   - Command (administrative action we will execute): update-route --route-id novacredit-credit-rationale --model seqclarity-v1.2 --force-pin
2) Canary with guardrails: If you want to test v1.4 while protecting live traffic, we do a 0.5% canary with hard safety filter and automated rollback if hallucination rate >0.3% on policy prompts.
3) Soft fix: apply a prompt-level safety wrapper (we can add a post-filter that rejects claims not supported by source docs). This reduces hallucination but adds ~40–80ms latency depending on corpus size.

Risk/impact tradeoffs:
- Pin to v1.2: immediate quality protection, preserves current latency/throughput, blocks v1.4 improvements until resolved.
- Canary + fix: lets you evaluate v1.4 benefits but requires close monitoring and an automated fallback (we can configure in Console).

I recommend pinning to v1.2 while we run a deeper root-cause test on v1.4. ETA for a short RCA + mitigation plan: 48 hours after pin.

I'll attach the diff report and a quick script to compute hallucination delta locally. Let me know if you want me to apply the pin now; I can make the change once Olivia confirms.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0123

Attachments: diff_report_v1.4_vs_v1.2.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: model-fit evals & regression concern — proposed pin/rollback options

Quick note on policy and rollout controls from engineering:

- We have a standard rollback + pin playbook. For enterprise customers with a compliance need, we can push a model pin at the routing-layer and add a time-bound annotation so the pin must be reviewed every 30 days.
- Canary automation: we will set up a canary job that computes hallucination delta and will auto-roll back v1.4 if the delta exceeds 0.3% over a sliding 1-hour window. The canary also streams traces to your SRE for auditing.
- Contract/terms: if Novacredit prefers strict version pinning as part of the Dedicated contract, Sales can add a short amendment to the EULA specifying allowed upgrade cadence. Camila — I can draft a short note for Legal and include a reference to the rollout_playbook.md in Drive.

Action items from engineering:
- If Olivia approves, Marcus to pin route to seqclarity-v1.2 (we'll run a smoke test).
- Engineering to run a 48-hour RCA on v1.4 and provide remediation plan + test harness to Novacredit.

Rishi
Head of Product | Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachment: rollout_playbook.md
